newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH PARLIAMENT APPROVES LAWS TO TACKLE FLOODS.
newsitem.headline: POLISH PARLIAMENT APPROVES LAWS TO TACKLE FLOODS.

text.p: Poland's lower house on Thursday approved laws to fund flood relief, including an amendment to the 1997 budget letting the government borrow more abroad and from the central bank, a parliament press office official said.
The budget amendment will increase by 2.5 billion zlotys the amount of treasury papers the government can sell directly to the central bank.
It also increases the limit on foreign borrowing to allow a $300 million soft loan Poland is seeking from the World Bank.

The measure was one of 21 being rushed through an emergency session of parliament to enable faster assistance to dozens of cities and hundreds of villages devastated by 10-day old floods that have struck the south of the country.
The bills included one that would rapidly provide every household directly struck by the catastrophe with 3,000 zlotys -- up from the 2,000 zlotys originally proposed.
The government earlier estimated that around 60,000 families would so far qualify for such aid.
The budget amendment increases to 4.5 billion zlotys from 3.0 billion the amount the government can borrow abroad this year, finance ministry spokeswoman Anna Sobocinska said.

The Senate, the upper house, was set to meet in late afternoon to examine the measures and parliamentary deputies said senators were likely to refrain from proposing any changes so as to speed their passage.

If the senate approves the bills, they will go to President Aleksander Kwasniewski for signing into law. Otherwise the lower house was scheduled for an evening session at which a third reading could be given.
Among the bills, one provides for farmers hit by the floods to be given one tonne of grain from state reserves for every hectare of affected land.
There are also measures to support housing construction and allow removal of customs duties on imports of vital goods such as building materials and sanitary equipment.
